name: Onion-skin motion trail

source.description: Two inspected references expose the path and timing of a move with fading ghost copies or trails.

technique: Ghost copies of a moving object, each a few frames behind, show the arc, spacing and easing of the move at once, the way an animator's onion skin does. Spacing between ghosts makes acceleration visible.
purpose: Teach or show motion: physics, easing, trajectories; add energy to a move.
visual_behaviour: A ball bounces or a dot travels with 3-5 translucent copies trailing it; the copies vanish when it settles.
mechanics: Clones replay the same motion function with a time lag (about 2 frames) and decreasing opacity; ghosts hidden after the move.

decomposition.timing: Ghost lag 1-3 frames; trail lifetime = the move plus 0.3 s.

failure_modes: Too many ghosts read as smear and cost DOM
Ghosts left on screen after the move
Ghosts of id-styled elements lose styling (style by class)

implementation.approach: Studio.space.trail(tl, target, at, motion, {count, lag, opacity, hold})

measurements.what: every-frame preview capture of tests/reference-derived/explainer-annotations (4 ghosts on a bounce)

provenance.observed: A bouncing ball and a dot on an arc leave ghost copies, with annotations about spacing and easing.
Dots travel with fading trails; an easing chart compares six ways to move between two points.

evidence.notes: Ghost stack visible during the baton's bounce, gone after.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
